item.title: NAMIC, Xceedance Launch Virtual Estimating
item.description: (Image source: IIR.) The National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies (NAMIC; Indianapolis) and Xceedance (Fort Lauderdale, Fla.) have launched the NAMIC Virtual Estimating Program Powered by Xceedance. “The Virtual Estimating Program offers NAMIC members the best of both state-of-the-art AI technology and valuable human expertise for a more accurate and efficient claims process.” AI-Enabled Estimating The program uses AI-enabled technology to support scope development, repair identification, documentation review and quality checks. The NAMIC-endorsed program is designed to help mutual insurers improve estimate quality, reduce turnaround times and expand estimating capacity across residential property, auto physical damage and farm equipment claims, according to a joint statement.

item.title: NHTSA Closes Rear-View Camera Probe into 129,000 Honda Vehicles
item.description: auto safety regulator on Tuesday closed an investigation into rear-view camera failures in 129,092 Honda Ridgeline pickup trucks, recalled in 2022, without further action. The agency said most reports it received involved other rear-view camera or wire-harness failure modes and could not be linked to the durability issue under investigation. The work found no rear-view camera failures caused by wire-harness damage, the agency said, and indicated that the part was not expected to fail during a reasonable vehicle lifespan.

item.title: Ex-Google Safety Chief Warns AI Could Harm Children More Than Social Media Did
item.description: The founder of the trust and safety team at Alphabet’s Google this week called for a slowdown in AI development, warning that the tech industry was repeating the same mistakes from the social media era, potentially causing even greater harm to children. “The idea that the industry will figure it out by itself without outside help is unrealistic.” Siegel’s concerns mirror a growing fear among some tech insiders and academic researchers that AI poses a deeper threat to children than social media did, at a time when the industry is racing to add increasingly advanced features to chatbots that millions of young people already use daily. Social media companies are paying huge sums and facing thousands of lawsuits over claims they harmed young users, while governments around the world are working to curb minors’ access to their platforms.

item.title: 60% expect property cat rates to fall, 86% expect T&Cs to loosen: Fitch reinsurance survey
item.description: Reinsurance companies are set to enter renewal negotiations from a position of capital strength, but the majority are expecting a challenging outcome, with prices expected to fall and terms and conditions expected to loosen further, a survey by Fitch Ratings found. In a survey carried out during the annual Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, Fitch Ratings found that reinsurance market conditions are driving underwriters to reduce their focus on property and property catastrophe risks, with fewer than 10% of respondents to its survey highlighting those lines of business as a high-priority for capital allocation. But, despite the fact reinsurers are saying their focus is elsewhere, conditions aren’t changing according to Fitch, who said that as capital supply continues to outpace demand for reinsurance protection the rating agency believes, “this factor will extend the buyer-friendly P&C market conditions, and increase pressure on reinsurers to achieve the best risk-adjusted returns with the lowest capital intensity.” 58% of respondents said that they expect terms and conditions will loosen selectively at the reinsurance renewals in 2027, with a further 28% saying they expect terms and conditions will loosen broadly and just 14% said T&Cs are expected to remain unchanged.

item.title: Direct institutional investor allocations to reinsurance grew at fastest rate in 2025: Marsh Re
item.description: Allocations to reinsurance grew fastest among direct institutional investors in 2025, outpacing the growth rate of assets deployed at independent insurance-linked securities managers and reinsurer sponsored managers, according to recent data from broker Marsh Re. But new information shared by Marsh Re shows that the growth rate has been different across the various cohorts of investor capital sources, with direct institutional investors growing their allocations to reinsurance at the fastest rate through 2025. Since 2013, when Marsh Re’s chart begins, the direct institutional investor bracket of allocators to reinsurance had been growing particularly slowly, but 2025 saw a meaningful uptick as it grew from $7 billion to $11 billion of the total third-party capital market.

item.title: Marsh and WEF call for place-based resilience to support insurability and reinsurance capacity
item.description: Marsh, a global insurance broking and risk management firm, and the World Economic Forum, an international organisation focused on public-private cooperation, are calling for greater investment in place-based resilience to support insurance and reinsurance availability and affordability as climate-related losses increase. The playbook, Addressing Insurability: A Playbook for Investing in Place-Based Resilience, says that conventional approaches often focus on protecting individual buildings or assets, while many of the risks affecting insurers and reinsurers extend beyond a single property. The organisations also distinguish between asset-level resilience and place-based resilience.

item.title: VIG expands telematics offering in CEE with Dolphin Technologies stake acquisition
item.description: Vienna Insurance Group (VIG), an Austria-based insurance group operating across Central and Eastern Europe (CEE), has acquired a 25% stake in Dolphin Technologies, a Vienna-based technology company. Founded in Vienna in 2001, Dolphin Technologies develops AI-powered telematics platforms and digital mobility services for insurance and automotive companies. Partnering with Dolphin enables VIG to continue broadening its market leadership in CEE telematics solutions, the firm stated.

item.title: CatIQ raises Montreal West Island flooding insured loss estimate to C$442m
item.description: CatIQ, Canada’s insured loss and exposure index provider, has raised its insurance industry loss estimate for the June 2026 flooding event that impacted Montreal’s West Island and the surrounding areas to CAD $442 million, a 7.5% increase from its second loss estimate of CAD $411 million that was issued in August. On June 20th and 21st, a series of thunderstorms struck Montreal’s West Island, as well as areas south of the city, flooding hundreds of properties. We covered CatIQ’s first loss estimate from the flooding event, where losses had reached CAD $409 million.

item.title: INTX expands Bermuda presence with Bespoke Analytics partnership

item.title: Pacific Hurricane Polo Is Now a Dangerous Category 5 Off Mexico
item.description: Hurricane Polo has become a dangerous Category 5 storm as it skirts Mexico’s southwest coast, and is expected to bring heavy rain across the region, the US National Hurricane Center said. Polo was about 360 miles (580 kilometers) south-southeast of the port city of Manzanillo, Mexico, with top winds of 160 miles per hour, the hurricane center said in its latest advisory. Polo is forecast to remain just offshore, sparing the country’s coastline another direct strike by a storm at the top of the five-step Saffir-Simpson hurricane wind scale.

item.title: DoorDash to Pay $132 Million in NYC Over Missing Wages
item.description: DoorDash Inc., the leading food-delivery firm in the US, said it agreed to a $131.5 million settlement with New York City to resolve a probe into its compliance with minimum-pay rules for couriers. The settlement, announced Tuesday, includes more than $83 million to resolve a disagreement over how to calculate pay for time that the workers spend online between deliveries, a requirement under the city’s rules. DoorDash is also paying $16.7 million in fines to the city’s Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, which enforces the pay rule.

item.title: Lawsuit Over Reese’s Halloween Pumpkins That Didn’t Resemble Packaging Dismissed
item.description: Hershey won the dismissal of a lawsuit claiming it let down consumers because its Halloween-themed Reese’s pumpkins lacked the decorative carved designs shown on the packaging. “Plaintiffs do not allege that the Hershey’s Reese’s Peanut Butter Pumpkins that they purchased were defective or worthless or that they lost all economic value because of the absence of the decorative carvings.” The judge also said Vidal and Granados could not show they paid up to 25% too much by citing Reese’s prices at Target, at Walmart and in Hershey’s online store, because they bought their candy at a Publix supermarket. Damian dismissed an earlier version of the lawsuit last September.

item.title: Drivers Widely Overestimate Driving Ability Despite Engaging in Risky Habits: Survey
item.description: drivers (85%) reported they’re safer than average, despite admitting risky habits, according to a new Arity survey. The survey reveals a disconnect between what drivers know is risky and the behaviors they report, highlighting the value of understanding driving behavior over time, the mobility and analytics provider said. A driving report can help reveal the patterns we may not see in ourselves, giving people a new way to understand how they really drive, not just how they think they drive.” Drivers’ perceptions of risk often differ depending on their own self-reported behavior.

item.title: Electronic Tolling, Better Signage Could Have Prevented Deadly Ohio Toll Plaza Crash
item.description: A deadly crash at a toll plaza on Interstate 80 near Swanton, Ohio, in 2024 could have been avoided if the turnpike used fully electronic tolling and provided clearer information about toll payment options, according to findings by the National Transportation Safety Board. NTSB investigators determined that the toll plaza’s hybrid design, which combines high-speed electronic tolling lanes with separated low-speed manual tolling lanes, increased the risk of a severe crash by creating conditions that encourage last-minute sudden lane changes and large speed differences between vehicles. On August 15, 2024, a crash occured the Swanton Township Toll Plaza on the Ohio Turnpike.

item.title: Casualty sidecars emerging as third pillar, sponsors urged to act: HCMA
item.description: Executives at Howden Capital Markets & Advisory (HCMA) have indicated that as traditional casualty capacity remains constrained, casualty sidecars are becoming a genuine third pillar alongside traditional reinsurance and the balance-sheet, moving beyond being a specialty product for a select number of sophisticated investors. Adding further insight, CEO Madea emphasised that this is the dynamic that HCMA wants its clients to think about when it comes to approaching casualty sidecars. HCMA, the capital markets and insurance-linked securities specialist unit of broking group Howden, recently conducted a roundtable, that explored the surge in momentum that’s being seen across the casualty reinsurance sidecar market.

item.title: GAINSCO unveils new brand

item.title: US Lawmakers Urge Trump to Maintain Ban on Chinese Automakers
item.description: More than two dozen Democratic lawmakers on Friday urged President Donald Trump to keep in place a ban on Chinese automakers out of the U.S. “We urge you to maintain strong protections against Chinese automobiles and connected vehicle technologies and ensure that China does not gain access to our market through direct imports, local production, and other avenues of circumvention,” said the 27 lawmakers led by Representative Debbie Dingell. Earlier this month, Trump told Fox News he would accept Chinese car companies building cars in the United States.
